c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: WHEATLAND TOWNSHIP ROAD MAINTENANCE MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: A Wheatland Township voted Road millage for two (2) mills terminates on December 31, 2025. Shall the expiring previous voted increase in the 15 mill tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes in Wheatland Township, of two (2) mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), be renewed at the original voted two (2) mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for four (4) years from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of building, repairing, maintaining, and constructing township roads, raising an estimated Seventy Five Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Nine Dollars and Zero Cents ($75,749.00) in the first year the millage is levied?

c.title: FIRE MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the expired previously voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Moore Township of 1 mil ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), be renewed at 1 mil ($ 1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levy it for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030, inclusive, to purchase firefighting equipment for the Moore Township Fire Department for the duration of the millage which will raise an estimated $37,500 in the first year the millage is levied?

c.title: GREENLEAF TOWNSHIP ROAD BRINE MILLAGE
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on all taxable property within Greenleaf Township, Sanilac County, Michigan be approved, the Township shall be authorized to levy annually a millage in the amount not to exceed 1.0 mill ($1.00 on each $1,000 of taxable value), on all real property located in Greenleaf Township, Sanilac County, Michigan for 4 years commencing January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2030, for the application of a second dirt road dust brine annually, instead of one.

c.title: ROAD MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: As a renewal of the rate previously approved by the electors which expired with the 2025 tax levy, shall the previously voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on all general ad valorem taxes within Evergreen Township be renewed at 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of 10 years, 2026 through 2035 inclusive, for the purpose of construction, improvement, dust control, and maintenance of roads in the Township, and shall the Township levy said millage which will raise an estimated $98,738 in the first year?

c.title: VILLAGE OF PECK
c.pre: PROPOSAL NO. 1 AUTHORIZATION TO SELL PORTION OF BARTLETT PARK PROPERTY
c.q: Shall the Village of Peck be authorized to sell the portion of Village-owned property currently comprising part of Bartlett Park and identified as a portion of Parcel No. 071-060-005-030-00 located south of the Spring Creek Drain, following approval of any necessary parcel split upon terms and conditions approved by the Village Council?

c.title: VILLAGE OF PECK
c.pre: PROPOSAL NO. 2 AUTHORIZATION TO SELL CERTAIN BARTLETT PARK PROPERTY
c.q: Shall the Village of Peck be authorized to sell the following Village-owned properties currently comprising part of Bartlett Park, upon terms and conditions approved by the Village Council: The portion of Parcel No. 071-060-005-030-00 located north of the Spring Creek Drain, following approval of any necessary parcel split; and Parcel No. 071-060-003-010-00?

c.title: SPEAKER TOWNSHP FIRE PROTECTION MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q:
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against taxable property in Speaker Township be increased by 2.0000 mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of six (6) years, 2027 through 2032, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for fire protection, including the purchase, replacement, maintenance, and improvement of fire trucks, fire apparatus, large equipment, air packs, and other equipment and facilities necessary to provide fire protection services, raising an estimated $110,000 in the first year if levied?

This proposal is for a new additional millage.

c.title: SPEAKER TOWNSHIP ROAD MAINTENANCE AND DUST CONTROL MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q:
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against taxable property in Speaker Township, Sanilac County, Michigan, be increased by 1.0000 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of six (6) years, 2027 through 2032, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for road maintenance, preservation, repair, construction and improvement, and dust control, including but not limited to road repairs, resurfacing, grading, gravel, drainage improvements, culvert work, dust abatement and control, and other necessary road-related improvements within the Township, raising an estimated $55,000 in the first year if levied?

This proposal is for a new additional millage.

c.title: Yale Public Schools Bond Proposal
c.q:
Shall Yale Public Schools, St. Clair and Sanilac Counties, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty Million Dollars ($20,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:

remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?

The following is for informational purposes only:

The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027, under current law, is 1.4 mills ($1.40 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is fourteen (14) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.48 mills ($2.48 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).

The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $11,900,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0.00. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.

(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)

c.title: LEXINGTON TOWNSHIP PROPOSAL TO APPROVE ROAD IMPROVEMENT MILLAGE
c.q:
Shall the expired previous voted millage increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Lexington Township of 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to .9933 mills by required millage rollbacks, be renewed and increased to up to 1.4933 mills ($1.4933 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for two (2) years (2026 through 2027 inclusive) for the purpose of road improvement, repair, and maintenance within the Township, raising an estimated $366,446.37 in the first year the millage is levied.

This is a specific dedicated millage for public roads purposes and funds raised may only be captured or used in cooperation with other local units of government taxing entities as allowed by law. The millage funds may be disbursed to multiple units of government service providers under agreements subject to change as the Township Board determines appropriate.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: PUBLIC SAFETY MILLAGE
c.q: For the purpose of raising funds to be used exclusively to maintain police and fire protection operations within the Village, shall the Constitutional Limitation upon the total amount of taxes which may be assessed in one year upon all taxable property located in the Village be increased by up to Three mills ($3 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of ten years from, 2026 through 2035, inclusive? If approved and levied in full, this millage will raise approximately $219,331.07 in its first year. Proceeds from the millage may be captured by tax increment financing authorities located with in the Village of Lexington if required by law.
